title: Acme Corp — Discovery Call
description: First call with Acme's platform team. Qualifying for the enterprise tier.
transcript: Dana, thanks for making the time. Can you hear me okay?
Loud and clear. Sorry, I'm dialling in from a hotel so if I drop out that's why.
No problem at all. I've got Elena with me — she leads customer success, so if this goes anywhere she's the person you'd actually be working with.
Hi Dana. Nice to meet you.
So I don't want to spend the call talking at you. Maybe start with what prompted you to reach out?
Sure. We've got about a hundred and forty people in the platform org, and we run a lot of meetings — probably too many, honestly.
The specific problem is that decisions get made in a call and then nobody can find them two weeks later. Someone takes notes, sometimes, and they end up in a doc nobody reads.
That's the exact pattern we hear most often. Is it all internal meetings, or customer-facing too?
Both, but internal is the painful one. Customer calls at least have a CRM entry.
Got it. And is anyone recording today?
Some teams record to Zoom cloud storage. Nobody watches them back. It's write-only.
That's very common. Recording solves the archival problem but not the retrieval problem.
Right, exactly. I don't need a video. I need to be able to search for 'did we decide to deprecate the v1 API' and get an answer.
That's essentially what the product does. Can I ask about your stack — what are you running for calendar and conferencing?
Google Workspace, and Meet for the most part. A few teams use Zoom because of a legacy contract that expires in March.
Both are supported. The Meet integration is the more mature one, for what it's worth.
Good, that's most of our volume.
Can I ask about compliance? A hundred and forty people in a platform org usually means someone in legal has opinions.
Ha. Yes. That's actually my main worry.
We're in a regulated segment for part of our business. Anything that records conversations has to go through a review, and that review has killed two tools already.
What killed them, specifically? Was it data residency, retention, or something else?
Residency mostly. One vendor couldn't tell us which region the audio was processed in, and that was the end of the conversation.
That's a fair thing to fail someone on.
It was less that the answer was wrong and more that they didn't seem to know. That's what worried the reviewers.
I'd rather flag this now than three weeks in — region pinning is available, but it's an enterprise-tier feature and it does affect the price.
That's fine. I'd rather pay for it than fail review again.
Then let's put the specifics in writing rather than me freelancing on a call. Elena, can you pull the data-handling doc together?
Yep. Dana, would it help if that covered retention and deletion as well? Those tend to come up in the same review.
It would, yes. Especially deletion. Our policy is ninety days for anything with customer data in it.
Ninety-day retention is configurable, so that's not a problem.
Can I ask about timeline? Is there something driving this, or is it a 'when we get to it'?
There's a driver. We've got a reorg landing in Q4 and I'd like the tooling in place before people start moving teams.
When someone changes team, all their context evaporates. That's the moment this hurts most.
So realistically you'd want to be live by — end of Q3?
Ideally, yes. Pilot in September, wider rollout in October.
That's achievable. The security review is usually the long pole, not the deployment.
How many people would be in the pilot?
I'd start with one team. Fifteen, maybe twenty.
That's a good size. Big enough to be a real test, small enough that you can actually talk to everyone about how it went.
What about budget — is there a number in mind, or does that come after the review?
There's a number but I'd rather not anchor on it before I know what the enterprise tier actually includes.
That's reasonable. I'll send pricing alongside the data-handling doc so you can look at them together.
One more thing worth raising — do you have a preference on whether the notetaker joins visibly, or records in the background?
Visibly. Strong preference. If people don't know they're being recorded that's its own compliance problem.
Good, that's the default. I only ask because some customers want the opposite and it's a difficult conversation.
Okay. So next steps from my side — Elena sends the data-handling and retention doc, I send enterprise pricing, and we get something in the diary for the week after next?
That works. I'll want to bring our security lead to the next one.
Please do. It's a much shorter process when they're in the room early.
Agreed. Send me the docs and I'll get them in front of him beforehand.
I'll have those over by Wednesday.
Great. Thanks both, this was useful.

summary.overview: Acme's platform organisation of roughly 140 people is losing decisions made in meetings — recordings exist but are effectively write-only. Dana's primary constraint is a compliance review that has already rejected two vendors, mainly on data residency, so region pinning and a ninety-day retention policy are requirements rather than preferences. A reorg landing in Q4 is driving the timeline: pilot with one team of 15–20 in September, wider rollout in October. Next steps are a data-handling document, enterprise pricing, and a follow-up call with Acme's security lead present.
summary.gist: Qualified enterprise opportunity; compliance review is the critical path, not deployment.

bullets: ~140 people in the platform org; decisions made in calls are unfindable two weeks later.
Internal meetings are the painful case — customer calls at least land in the CRM.
Existing Zoom recordings are archival only; nobody watches them back.
Two prior vendors were rejected in review, primarily on data residency.
One failed because they could not say which region audio was processed in — the uncertainty, not the answer, was disqualifying.
Region pinning is enterprise-tier and affects price; Dana accepted that trade readily.
Acme policy is ninety-day retention for anything containing customer data.
Configurable retention covers this; deletion behaviour must be documented explicitly.
A Q4 reorg is the forcing function — team moves are when lost context hurts most.
Pilot one team of 15–20 in September, wider rollout October.
Security review is the long pole; deployment is not.

action_items.text: Send Acme the data-handling, residency and retention document
Send enterprise tier pricing including region pinning
Book a follow-up call with Acme's security lead present
